newsitem.title: CHILE: Pinochet drops charges against Chilean Communist.
newsitem.headline: Pinochet drops charges against Chilean Communist.

text.p: Former Chilean military ruler Augusto Pinochet withdrew his slander charges against the head of Chile's Communist Party on Thursday after her arrest drew angry criticism.

Communist Party President Gladys Marin walked out of a Santiago courthouse two days after police arrested her on slander and defamation charges for calling Pinochet a blackmailer and a pyschopath in September.
She was freed after Pinochet, currently army commander-in- chief, dropped the charges, court officials said.
"What the army has shown is that it was defeated, because it did not speak the truth," Marin told reporters as hundreds of cheering, banner-waving supporters crowded around her.

Marin's arrest brought a torrent of criticism from top Chilean politicians, including many in President Eduardo Frei's government, and from the Cuban government, which called Marin "a worthy friend who was always in solidarity with Cuba."
Chilean officials had said the arrest would tarnish the country's reputation barely a week before 20 foreign heads of state, including Cuba's Fidel Castro, arrive for an Ibero-American summit.
Local news reports said Defence Minister Edmundo Perez Yoma personally asked Pinochet to withdraw the charges.
Marin's supporters held day and night rallies for her outside the detention centre, some of them waving placards with the offending words, followed by "Send me to jail too."
